axes.model_access:
**The official API backend for ExLlamaV3** — the README says "TabbyAPI is also the official API backend server for Exllamav3":
it runs local weights supported by ExLlamaV3 (the exllamav3 backend) such as GPTQ/GGUF, not a service calling an external model.
Model files live in a local directory mounted into the process (Docker wording: mount the models directory into the container).
axes.runtime:
A **FastAPI local server** (Python 3.10–3.14); the official CUDA image is on GHCR (ghcr.io/theroyallab/tabbyapi),
tags latest (CUDA 12.8)/cu13/latest-rocm (AMD RX 7900 series)/latest-extras (with the optional embeddings stack).
GitHub theroyallab/tabbyAPI AGPL-3.0 1,502 stars, pushed 2026-10-30 (API verified);
**GitHub releases count is 0 — releases follow a rolling-release model (README self-description); the change-record line is commits**.
axes.local_files: Reads and writes local files — the model-weights directory, config.yml; the API defaults to localhost:5000.
axes.background:
A persistent local process (FastAPI server); no persistent cloud surface. The README disclaimer self-describes it as a "hobby project…not meant to run
on production servers" — for production workloads the official advice is to look elsewhere.
axes.tools:
An OpenAI-compatible API surface (chat/completions and similar endpoints) + an admin surface (admin UI/status page; admin features visible evolving in commits);
not an agent-tool host — it is an inference-API server for frontends (SillyTavern-style) or clients.
axes.context:
No cross-session memory (it is an inference-serving surface) — context length follows the ExLlamaV3 backend config (max_context-style parameters);
conversation state is carried by the frontend client (SillyTavern-style); the server stores no chat history.
axes.permissions:
Runs locally; an API key can be configured (config.yml); the permission surface = local files and GPU. The Docker wording requires a larger --shm-size
(ExLlamaV3 uses POSIX shared memory for tensor parallelism and CPU MoE offload; the 64 MiB default is not enough — stated plainly in the README).
axes.fit:
Fits: the ExLlamaV3 ecosystem (GPTQ-family quantization) wanting an OpenAI-compatible API — the standard answer; one-shot Docker CUDA/ROCm inference servers.
Does not fit: production-grade serving (officially self-described as not production-oriented — that is the vLLM/TGI line); broad GGUF quant coverage (the llama.cpp root).

runs: This site has not completed measured runs. The test protocol is at [protocols/runner/_protocol.md](../../../protocols/runner/_protocol.md).
unknowns:
- The full quantization-format support matrix (per-tier GPTQ/GGUF support; the Wiki has wording, not verified item by item)
- All config.yml options (API key, admin-surface toggles, etc.; not enumerated item by item)
- What the embeddings stack (latest-extras) actually covers (mentioned in the README, not verified)
related: Contrast: llama.cpp is the GGUF inference root; TabbyAPI stands on the ExLlamaV3 backend (strong on the GPTQ family).
Contrast: Ollama is a productized pull-and-run wrapper; TabbyAPI is an API server for frontends, with a more engineering-oriented configuration surface.
Same family: both belong to the local-inference-server + web-admin ecosystem; TabbyAPI has no UI shell — it is a pure API server.
Boundary contrast: a cloud chat entry vs a local ExLlamaV3 inference API — both OpenAI-compatible endpoints, completely different data boundaries and model ownership.
